title: Changing the purpose of the corporation to rebalance capitalism
Climate in the Boardroom: Struggling to reconcile business as usual and the end of the world as we know it
abstract: How does one witness to businesspeople about climate change? Climate change is a problem for the collective and the long term, whereas business often requires a ruthless focus on the individual and the quarter. Climate change is an ethical catastrophe whose solution almost certainly requires a profoundly moral response, but talk of morality in the boardroom is often regarded with profound suspicion. Reconciling these tensions has forced me to navigate between worlds in an ongoing attempt to persuade businesspeople that solving climate change is both an economic and a moral necessity, and that the purpose of business is not only to make money but also to support the institutions that will enable us to build a sustainable world. This has not always been easy.
abstract_zh: 如何向商界人士阐明气候变化问题？气候变化是一个关乎集体和长远的问题，而企业往往需要对个体和季度业绩保持冷酷的专注。气候变化是一场伦理灾难，其解决几乎必然需要深刻的道德回应，然而在董事会上谈论道德往往遭到强烈怀疑。调和这些张力，迫使我在不同的世界之间游走，不断努力说服商界人士：解决气候变化既是经济上的必需，也是道德上的必需；企业的目的不仅在于赚钱，也在于支持那些能够使我们建设可持续世界的制度。这一过程并不总是容易的。

title: Innovation in the 21st Century: Architectural change, purpose, and the challenges of our time
Reimagining Capitalism in a World on Fire
Tackling Climate Change Requires Organizational Purpose
venue: American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings, 110: 177-180
abstract: The public debate about how to tackle climate change has been overwhelmingly dominated by the assumption that it can be solved through the adoption of an appropriate pricing regime. This paper argues that while the development of such a regime will be critical to slowing climate change, it is a necessary, but not a sufficient, condition. We argue that it will also be important to accelerate rates of innovation and cooperation across the economy and that one important tool for doing this is the active encouragement of the development of authentically “purpose-driven” organizations.
abstract_zh: 关于如何应对气候变化的公共辩论，长期以来几乎完全被一种假设所主导：即可以通过采用适当的定价机制来解决这一问题。本文认为，尽管建立这样的机制对于减缓气候变化至关重要，但它只是必要条件，而非充分条件。我们认为，加快整个经济中的创新速度与合作水平同样重要，而实现这一目标的一个重要工具，是积极鼓励发展真正“以目标为导向”的组织。

Making the Business Case for Environmental Sustainability
venue: Leading Sustainable Change (eds. Henderson, Gulati, Tushman), Oxford University Press
abstract: Can a business case be made for acting sustainably? This is a difficult question to answer precisely, largely because there is no generally accepted definition of the term “sustainability”. Is it acting sustainably to protect the human rights of the firm’s workforce? To invest in education in local communities? To switch to renewable power? All of these actions might improve social welfare, and some of them might improve profitability but they are very different, and the business case for each of them is similarly likely to look quite different. Here I begin to explore the issue by focusing on a more limited question, namely whether a business case be made for acting in an environmentally sustainable way, which I define as acting in any way that reduce a firm’s environmental footprint.
abstract_zh: 企业能否为可持续地经营提供商业理由？这个问题很难精确回答，很大程度上是因为“可持续性”一词并没有普遍接受的定义。保护企业员工的人权算不算可持续行为？投资于当地社区的教育算不算？转向可再生能源算不算？这些行动都可能改善社会福利，其中一些还可能提高盈利能力，但它们彼此之间差异很大，每一项的商业理由也很可能大不相同。本文通过聚焦一个更有限的问题，开始对这一议题展开探讨，即企业是否可以为以环境可持续的方式经营提供商业理由。我这里将环境可持续定义为任何能够减少企业环境足迹的经营方式。

title: Accelerating Energy Innovation: Insights from Multiple Sectors (edited volume)
venue: NBER and University of Chicago Press
abstract: Accelerating energy innovation could be an important part of an effective response to the threat of climate change. Written by a stellar group of experts in the field, this book complements existing research on the subject with an exploration of the role that public and private policy have played in enabling - and sustaining - swift innovation in a variety of industries, from agriculture and the life sciences to information technology. Chapters highlight the factors that have determined the impact of past policies and suggest that effectively managed federal funding, strategies to increase customer demand, and the enabling of aggressive competition from new firms are important ingredients for policies that affect innovative activity.
abstract_zh: 加快能源创新可能是应对气候变化威胁的有效举措的重要组成部分。本书由该领域一批杰出专家撰写，通过探讨公共与私人政策在促进并维持各类行业（从农业、生命科学到信息技术）快速创新中所发挥的作用，对该主题的现有研究形成了补充。各章节重点阐述了决定既往政策影响的因素，并指出，有效管理的联邦资金、刺激客户需求的策略，以及允许新企业展开激烈竞争，是影响创新活动政策的重要组成要素。

venue: Technological Innovation: Oversights and Foresights (eds. Garud, Nayyar, Shapira), Cambridge University Press
abstract: Introduction Accurate technological forecasting is extraordinarily important. It can allow managers to shape technology strategy, to prevent continued investment in technologies that are long past their prime, and to guard against premature commitment to untried technologies whose long-term potential is limited. Unfortunately, accurate technological forecasting is notoriously difficult (see some of the other chapters in this volume). In this chapter, I hope to contribute to the practice of technological forecasting through a detailed analysis of the usefulness of one tool that has been widely advanced as a guide to technological foresight: the technology life cycle (Van Wyk, 1985). I use the history of optical photolithographic alignment technology to suggest that the uncritical application of the life cycle as a forecasting tool may have quite dangerous implications. The life cycle is a useful ex post descriptive device: appropriate proscriptive use of it requires a detailed understanding of the underlying technological, economic, and social dynamics on which it rests, in combination with a critical awareness of the ways in which industry acceptance of the life cycle as a descriptive tool can obscure these dynamics, making it very difficult to use it with any accuracy. Industry pundits have been confidently using the technological life cycle to predict the death of optical photolithography since 1977, yet it remains the tool of choice in leading-edge semiconductor production (Figure 9.1). The factors that lie behind this singularly unsuccessful forecasting effort throw considerable light on the limits of the technological life cycle as a forecasting tool.
abstract_zh: 引言：准确的技术预测极为重要。它能够使管理者塑造技术战略，防止对早已过时的技术持续投资，并防范过早承诺于长期潜力有限的未经检验的技术。遗憾的是，准确的技术预测以困难著称（参见本书其他章节）。在本章中，我希望通过详细分析一种被广泛推崇为技术前瞻指南的工具的有用性，为技术预测的实践作出贡献：即技术生命周期（Van Wyk，1985）。我借助光学光刻对准技术的历史表明，不加批判地将生命周期用作预测工具，可能会带来相当危险的后果。生命周期是一种有用的事后描述性工具：对其进行恰当的规范性使用，需要详细理解其所依托的技术、经济与社会动态，同时也需要批判性地认识到，行业对生命周期作为描述性工具的接受，可能会掩盖这些动态，从而使得准确地运用它变得十分困难。自1977年以来，行业专家们便自信地运用技术生命周期预测光学光刻的消亡，然而它至今仍是尖端半导体生产中的首选工具（图9.1）。这一极为不成功的预测努力背后的各种因素，充分揭示了技术生命周期作为预测工具的局限性。
